title: Identifying people in a photograph of the later Tonic Triad
summary: Looking at a photograph, Clark identifies Pritchett, the Hamiltons, Oscar Henry, Albert Francis, Peter Rayfield and others.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: Maybe if we stopped and got the picture, we could refresh your memory a little bit that way, would that help? There's a picture, hand in some place, do you know where it is?
Charlie. We can move this. Go, go, go there and get that picture hanging up over there. Tony, that's not the old Tony tried. What year? Oh, I don't know, this was a year. The hair that colored there.
Was it after depression?

Oh yes, this was after depression. Now, you see, this is Pritchett. On the extreme right standing. This is Professor Dalmers. That's the bass player. Bass drum. That's the one that didn't show up on this job and caused me to switch the bass. He's the bass. Now that's Willie Pazio. No.
Yeah. That's Landry. I mean Landry.
That's Landry rather. This is Willie Pazio.
That's Peter Rayfield.
Who's the trumpet player that's kneeling? You know him?
Yeah. Now let me get my pencil off on it. That fellow there. Oh, I don't know him. That's why I tell you there's something that I don't know.
Now this is, this fellow here is Loomis Hamilton. That's George Hamilton's son. This is Bell. Well let's back up. He's a baritone.
Who was George Hamilton?
George Hamilton is this fellow. He plays what?
He played bass. He played bass and Loomis Hamilton played trumpet. Trumpet, yeah.
Now the baritone. And this is Oscar Henry. And this is a Lopis boy. His daddy runs that Undertaker place down on Dumaine Street.
He's a trombone player?

Yeah, he's a trombone, but I think he gave it up. And that's me. And this is Albert Warner. Now this fellow's name is Parnaret. That's a clarinet player. Now this is Albert Francis, the one I told you about.
Yes.
See?
Snare drum.
And this is Peter Rayfield. He played the bass drum.
Who was that baritone player there?

Bell. He was crippling his right arm. He used to finger that horn with his left hand. He had an arm drawn up from one side. I don't know, he said he had to fall off a horse when he was a boy and it affected his arm and drew it up.
I know that fellow.
That's old man Barberang.
Is it though? Yeah.
It looked old then too, didn't it?
Yeah.
Were these fellas playing?

All those fellas just were standing around. Where was this taken, did you tell us? That's taken out there in where, out there in Jefferson where the old racetrack, old racetrack used to be. Not this new one they built, the old one they had. That's why I say it's years back.
You had three saxophones, four. Yeah. Two girls and two boys. They looked quite young.
Well that's those Grisby girls.
Are they related to Pritchard or are they?
No, he works in their father's tailor shop.
I know he said Grisby and Grisby.
Yeah that's right, well those are Grisby girls.
And these two boys? Well I don't know them.
See these fellas, I don't know those at all. I tell you a lot of them in there I don't know.
One boy may be playing a tenor and the other alto, I can't see too well. Where? Here, tenor saxophone and alto.
No, that's alto. Alto.
All four of them are alto saxophone? Alto, yeah.
That kid looks familiar to me. I don't know who that kid is. Fair enough.
He looks like a trumpet player, Red Russo.
He looks like Red Russo the trumpet player, that's funny.
